paragraphs: Credit Acceptance Corporation (referred to as the "Company", "Credit Acceptance", "we", "our" or "us") makes vehicle ownership possible by providing innovative financing solutions that enable automobile dealers to sell vehicles to consumers, regardless of their credit history. Our financing programs are offered through a nationwide network of automobile dealers who benefit from sales of vehicles to consumers who otherwise could not obtain financing; from repeat and referral sales generated by these same customers; and from sales to customers responding to advertisements for our financing programs, but who actually end up qualifying for traditional financing.

Without our financing programs, consumers are often unable to purchase vehicles or they purchase unreliable ones. Further, as we report to the three national credit reporting agencies, an important ancillary benefit of our programs is that we provide consumers with an opportunity to improve their lives by improving their credit score and move on to more traditional sources of financing.

Credit Acceptance was founded in 1972 to collect retail installment contracts (referred to as "Consumer Loans") originated by automobile dealerships owned by Donald Foss, our founder. During the 1980s, we began to market this service to non-affiliated dealers and, at the same time, began to offer dealers a non-recourse cash payment (referred to as an "advance") against anticipated future collections on Consumer Loans serviced for that dealer.

We refer to automobile dealers who participate in our programs and who share our desire to provide an opportunity to consumers to improve their lives as "Dealers." Upon enrollment in our financing programs, the Dealer enters into a Dealer servicing agreement with us that defines the legal relationship between Credit Acceptance and the Dealer. The Dealer servicing agreement assigns the responsibilities for administering, servicing, and collecting the amounts due on Consumer Loans from the Dealers to us. We are an indirect lender from a legal perspective, meaning the Consumer Loan is originated by the Dealer and assigned to us.

The majority of the Consumer Loans assigned to us are made to consumers with impaired or limited credit histories. The following table shows the percentage of Consumer Loans assigned to us with either FICO® scores below 650 or no FICO® scores:

We currently operate in one reportable segment which represents our core business of offering innovative financing solutions and related products and services that enable Dealers to sell vehicles to consumers regardless of their credit history. For information regarding our one reportable segment and related disclosures, see Note 14 to the consolidated financial statements contained in Item 8 of this Form 10-K, which is incorporated herein by reference.

We offer Dealers financing programs that enable them to sell vehicles to consumers, regardless of their credit history. We have two programs: the Portfolio Program and the Purchase Program. Under the Portfolio Program, we advance money to Dealers (referred to as a "Dealer Loan") in exchange for the right to service the underlying Consumer Loans. Under the Purchase Program, we buy the Consumer Loans from the Dealers (referred to as a "Purchased Loan") and keep all amounts collected from the consumer. Dealer Loans and Purchased Loans are collectively referred to as "Loans." The following table shows the percentage of Consumer Loans assigned to us under each of the programs for each of the last three years:

(1)Represents advances paid to Dealers on Consumer Loans assigned under the Portfolio Program and one-time payments made to Dealers to purchase Consumer Loans assigned under the Purchase Program. Payments of Dealer Holdback (as defined below) and accelerated Dealer Holdback are not included.
As payment for the vehicle, the Dealer generally receives the following: •a down payment from the consumer;

•after the advance balance (cash advance and related Dealer Loan fees and costs) has been recovered by us, the cash from payments made on the Consumer Loan, net of certain collection costs and our servicing fee ("Dealer Holdback").

We record the amount advanced to the Dealer as a Dealer Loan, which is classified within Loans receivable in our consolidated balance sheets. Cash advanced to the Dealer is automatically assigned to the Dealer's open pool of advances. Dealers make an election as to how many Consumer Loans (either 50 or 100) will be assigned to an open pool before it is closed, and subsequent advances are assigned to a new pool. Unless we receive a request from the Dealer to keep a pool open, we automatically close each pool based on the Dealer's election. All advances within a Dealer's pool are secured by the future collections on the related Consumer Loans assigned to the pool. For Dealers with more than one pool, the pools are cross-collateralized so the performance of other pools is considered in determining eligibility for Dealer Holdback. We perfect our security interest with respect to the Dealer Loans by obtaining control or taking possession of the Consumer Loans, which list us as lien holder on the vehicle title.

headings: Industry, Operational, and Macroeconomic Risks
Our inability to accurately forecast and estimate the amount and timing of future collections could have a material adverse effect on results of operations.
Due to competition from traditional financing sources and non-traditional lenders, we may not be able to compete successfully.
Reliance on third parties to administer our ancillary product offerings could adversely affect our business and financial results.
We are dependent on our senior management, and the loss of any of these individuals or an inability to hire additional team members could adversely affect our ability to operate profitably.
Our reputation is a key asset to our business, and our business may be affected by how we are perceived in the marketplace.
An outbreak of contagious disease or other public health emergency could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations.
The concentration of Dealers in several states could adversely affect us.
Reliance on our outsourced business functions could adversely affect our business.
Our ability to hire and retain foreign engineering personnel could be hindered by immigration restrictions.
We may be unable to execute our business strategy due to current economic conditions.
Governmental or market responses to climate change and related environmental issues could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Capital and Liquidity Risks
We may be unable to continue to access or renew funding sources and obtain capital needed to maintain and grow our business.
The terms of our debt limit how we conduct our business.
A violation of the terms of our Term ABS financings or Warehouse facilities could have a material adverse impact on our operations.
Our substantial debt could negatively impact our business, prevent us from satisfying our debt obligations, and adversely affect our financial condition.
We may not be able to generate sufficient cash flows to service our outstanding debt and fund operations and may be forced to take other actions to satisfy our obligations under such debt.
Interest rate fluctuations may adversely affect our borrowing costs, profitability, and liquidity.

Reduction in our credit rating could increase the cost of our funding from, and restrict our access to, the capital markets and adversely affect our liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations.
We may incur substantially more debt and other liabilities. This could exacerbate further the risks associated with our current debt levels.
Technology and Cybersecurity Risks
Our dependence on technology could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Our use of electronic contracts could impact our ability to perfect our ownership or security interest in Consumer Loans.

Failure to properly safeguard our proprietary business information or confidential consumer and team member personal information could subject us to liability, decrease our profitability, and damage our reputation.
The development and use of artificial intelligence presents risks and challenges that may adversely impact our business.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
Litigation we are involved in from time to time may adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.
Changes in tax laws and the resolution of uncertain income tax matters could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and cash flows from operations.
The regulations to which we are or may become subject could result in a material adverse effect on our business.
paragraphs: The majority of the Consumer Loans assigned to us are made to individuals with impaired or limited credit histories. Consumer Loans made to these individuals generally entail a higher risk of delinquency, default, and repossession, and higher losses than loans made to consumers with better credit. Since most of our revenue and cash flows from operations are generated from these Consumer Loans, our ability to accurately forecast Consumer Loan performance is critical to our business and financial results. At the time of assignment, we forecast future expected cash flows from the Consumer Loan. Based on these forecasts, which include estimates for wholesale vehicle prices in the event of vehicle repossession and sale, we make an advance or one-time purchase payment to the related Dealer at a level designed to maximize economic profit, a non-GAAP financial measure. We continue to forecast the expected collection rate for each Consumer Loan subsequent to assignment. These forecasts also serve as a critical assumption in our accounting for recognizing finance charge income and determining our allowance for credit losses. Please see the Critical Accounting Estimates – Finance Charge Revenue & Allowance for Credit Losses section in Item 7 of this Form 10-K, which is incorporated herein by reference. Actual cash flows from any individual Consumer Loan are often different from cash flows estimated at the time of assignment. There can be no assurance that our forecasts will be accurate or that Consumer Loan performance will be as expected. In periods with changing economic conditions, accurately forecasting the performance of Consumer Loans is more difficult. In the event that our forecasts are not accurate in the aggregate, our financial position, liquidity, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.

The automobile finance market for consumers who do not qualify for conventional automobile financing is large and highly competitive. The market is served by a variety of companies, including "buy here, pay here" dealerships. The market is also currently served by banks, captive finance affiliates of automobile manufacturers, credit unions, and independent finance companies both publicly and privately owned. Many of these companies are much larger and have greater financial resources than are available to us, and many have long-standing relationships with automobile dealerships. Providers of automobile financing have traditionally competed based on the interest rate charged, the quality of credit accepted, the flexibility of loan terms offered, and the quality of service provided to dealers and consumers. We may be unable to compete successfully in the automobile finance market or, due to the intense competition in this market, our results of operations, cash flows, and financial condition may be adversely affected as we adjust our business in response to competitive pressures. Increasing advance rates on Loans has the impact of reducing the return on capital we expect to earn on Loans. Additionally, if we are unsuccessful in maintaining and expanding our relationships with Dealers, we may be unable to accept Consumer Loans in the volume and on the terms that we anticipate.

Adverse changes in economic conditions, the automobile or finance industries, or the non-prime consumer market could adversely affect our financial position, liquidity, and results of operations, the ability of key vendors that we depend on to supply us with services, and our ability to enter into future financing transactions.

We are subject to general economic conditions which are beyond our control. During periods of economic slowdown or recession, delinquencies, defaults, repossessions, and losses may increase on our Consumer Loans, and Consumer Loan prepayments, which historically have been lower in periods with less availability of consumer credit, may decline. These periods are also typically accompanied by decreased consumer demand for automobiles and declining values of automobiles securing outstanding Consumer Loans, which weakens collateral coverage and increases the amount of loss in the event of default. Significant increases in the inventory of used automobiles during periods of economic recession may also depress the prices at which repossessed automobiles may be sold or delay the timing of these sales. Additionally, inflation, higher gasoline prices, the deferral or resumption of student loan payments, increased focus on climate-related initiatives and regulation, declining stock market values, unstable real estate values, resets of adjustable rate mortgages to higher interest rates, increasing unemployment levels, general availability of consumer credit, tariffs, or other factors that impact consumer confidence or disposable income could increase loss frequency and decrease consumer demand for automobiles as well as weaken collateral values of automobiles. Imposition of or increases in tariffs on U.S. imports could result in higher used car prices in the United States, leading to decreased Dealer origination of Consumer Loans and a decline in Consumer Loan assignments to us. Because our business is focused on consumers who do not qualify for conventional automobile financing, the actual rates of delinquencies, defaults, repossessions, and losses on our Consumer Loans could be higher than those experienced in the general automobile finance industry, and could be more dramatically affected by a general economic downturn.

We rely on Dealers to originate Consumer Loans for assignment under our programs. High levels of Dealer attrition, due to a general economic downturn or otherwise, could materially adversely affect our operations. In addition, we rely on vendors to provide us with services we need to operate our business. Any disruption in our operations due to the untimely or discontinued supply of these services could substantially adversely affect our operations. Finally, during an economic slowdown or recession, our servicing costs may increase without a corresponding increase in finance charge revenue. Any sustained period of increased delinquencies, defaults, repossessions, or losses or increased servicing costs could also materially adversely affect our financial position, liquidity, and results of operations and our ability to enter into future financing transactions.

Technological advancements or changes to trends in the automobile industry such as new autonomous driving technologies or car- and ride-sharing programs could decrease consumer demand for automobiles. Decreased consumer demand for automobiles could negatively impact demand for our financing programs as well as weaken collateral values of automobiles, which could materially adversely affect our financial position, liquidity, and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and related notes contained in Item 8 of this Form 10-K, which is incorporated herein by reference.

We make vehicle ownership possible by providing innovative financing solutions that enable automobile dealers to sell vehicles to consumers, regardless of their credit history. Our financing programs are offered through a nationwide network of automobile dealers who benefit from sales of vehicles to consumers who otherwise could not obtain financing; from repeat and referral sales generated by these same customers; and from sales to customers responding to advertisements for our financing programs, but who actually end up qualifying for traditional financing.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, consolidated net income was $423.9 million, or $36.38 per diluted share, compared to $247.9 million, or $19.88 per diluted share, for the same period in 2024. The increase in consolidated net income was primarily due to a decrease in provision for credit losses and an increase in finance charges, partially offset by an increase in operating expenses. Our results for the year ended December 31, 2025 included:
•$8.0 billion average balance of our Loan portfolio, which represented a 5.7% increase from 2024.
•A 12.6% and 16.5% year-over-year decline in Consumer Loan unit and dollar volumes, respectively, as compared to 2024.
•$169.5 million, or 1.5%, decrease in forecasted net cash flows from our Loan portfolio, which represented a smaller decrease compared to 2024.
•$725.4 million in the repurchase of approximately 1,514,000 shares, or 12.6% of the shares outstanding at the beginning of the year.
•The enrollment of 5,752 new Dealers, with 15,745 active Dealers during 2025, which is our highest ever number of active Dealers in a calendar year.
•$230.8 million in Dealer Holdback and accelerated Dealer Holdback payments to Dealers.
•$74.2 million contingent loss related to previously disclosed legal matters.
•$1.7 billion in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and unused and available revolving lines of credit as of December 31, 2025.

•12 workplace awards, including reaching #34 on Great Place to Work® and Fortune magazine's 100 Best Companies to Work For® list and #2 on the 2025 Top Workplaces USA list in the 1,000-2,499 employee company size category.

For the year ended December 31, 2024, consolidated net income was $247.9 million, or $19.88 per diluted share, compared to $286.1 million, or $21.99 per diluted share, for the same period in 2023. The decrease in consolidated net income was primarily due to increases in interest expense and provision for credit losses, partially offset by an increase in finance charges. Our results for the year ended December 31, 2024 included:
•$7.5 billion average balance of our Loan portfolio, which represented a 13.6% increase from 2023.

paragraphs: Credit Acceptance Corporation (referred to as the "Company", "Credit Acceptance", "we", "our" or "us") 提供創新融資方案，使汽車經銷商能將車輛銷售給消費者，不管其信用記錄如何。我們的融資方案透過全國經銷商網路提供，這些經銷商能從銷售給原本無法取得融資的消費者、這些消費者產生的重複及推薦銷售，以及回應我們融資方案廣告的消費者實際符合傳統融資條件的銷售中受益。
若沒有我們的融資方案，消費者往往無法購買車輛或只能購買不可靠的車輛。此外，因為我們向三大國家信用報告機構報告，我們方案的重要附屬好處是，我們為消費者提供改善生活機會，透過提高其信用分數，進而轉向更傳統的融資來源。
Credit Acceptance 於 1972 年成立，目的是收購由 Donald Foss 所擁有汽車經銷商所發行的零售分期付款合約（稱為 "Consumer Loans"）。在 1980 年代，我們開始將此服務行銷給非關係企業經銷商，同時也開始為經銷商提供非追索權現金付款（稱為 "advance"），以對應預期未來收付款的 Consumer Loans。
我們稱參與我們方案並希望為消費者提供改善生活機會的汽車經銷商為 "Dealers"。經銷商加入我們的融資方案時，會與我們簽訂經銷商服務協議，以界定 Credit Acceptance 與經銷商之間的法律關係。經銷商服務協議將管理、服務及收取 Consumer Loans 金額的責任指派給我們。我們從法律觀點而言是間接貸款人，表示 Consumer Loan 由經銷商發行並轉讓給我們。
我們所接收的 Consumer Loans 多數是針對信用記錄受損或信用記錄有限的消費者。下表顯示我們接收的 Consumer Loans 中，FICO® 分數低於 650 或無 FICO® 分數的比例：
FICO® 分數低於 650 或無 FICO® 分數的總單位銷售量百分比 79.5 % 80.6 % 80.9 %
我們目前只有一個應報告分部，代表我們的核心業務，即提供創新融資方案及相關產品與服務，使經銷商能將車輛銷售給不管其信用記錄如何的消費者。有關我們一個應報告分部及相關揭露資訊，請參閱本 Form 10-K 第 8 項所附整併財務報表的附註 14，此附註已於 herein 進行參考。

我們為經銷商提供融資方案，使他們能將車輛銷售給不管其信用記錄如何的消費者。我們有兩個方案：Portfolio Program 與 Purchase Program。在 Portfolio Program 下，我們向經銷商提供資金（稱為 "Dealer Loan"），以換取服務基礎 Consumer Loans 的權利。在 Purchase Program 下，我們從經銷商處購買 Consumer Loans（稱為 "Purchased Loan"），並保留從消費者收取的所有金額。Dealer Loans 與 Purchased Loans 合稱為 "Loans"。下表顯示我們在每個方案下接收的 Consumer Loans 在過去三年的比例：

作為車輛的付款，經銷商通常會收到以下項目：• 消費者所支付的首付款；
• 在我們收回預付款餘額（現金預付款及相關經銷商貸款費用及成本）後，來自消費者貸款的現金支付，扣除部分收款成本及我們的服務費用（"經銷商保留款"）。

我們將支付給經銷商的金額記為經銷商貸款，此項貸款會歸類於我們合併財務報表中的應收貸款。支付給經銷商的現金會自動分配至經銷商的開放貸款池。經銷商會決定將多少筆消費者貸款（為 50 或 100 筆）分配至開放貸款池，直到該池關閉為止，隨後的貸款會分配至新的貸款池。除非經銷商向我們提出要求維持貸款池開放，否則我們會根據經銷商的選擇自動關閉每個貸款池。每個經銷商貸款池內的所有貸款均以相關消費者貸款的未來收款作為擔保。對於擁有超過一個貸款池的經銷商，這些貸款池會交叉擔保，因此其他貸款池的表現會被納入評估經銷商保留款資格的考量。我們透過取得控制權或實際持有消費者貸款，以確保對經銷商貸款的優先受償權，這些貸款會列明我們為車輛所有權的擔保人。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應與本表單 10-K 第 8 項所載之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀，該部分已於 herein by reference 並入本文件。
我們透過提供創新融資方案，使車輛所有權成為可能，讓汽車經銷商能將車輛銷售給消費者，不管其信用記錄如何。我們的融資方案透過全國性的汽車經銷商網路提供，這些經銷商從銷售給原本無法取得融資的消費者中受益；從這些消費者產生的重複銷售與推薦銷售中受益；以及從回應我們融資方案廣告的消費者中受益，但這些消費者最終實際上符合傳統融資的條件。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止之會計年度，合併淨收入為 423.9 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後 36.38 美元，與 2024 年同期的 247.9 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後 19.88 美元相比。合併淨收入的增加主要是由於信貸損失提撥減少，以及融資費用增加，部分抵銷了營運費用增加的影響。我們截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止之會計年度結果包括：
• 我們貸款組合的平均餘額為 8.0 十億美元，較 2024 年成長 5.7%。
• 消費貸款單位數與金額較 2024 年分別年減 12.6% 與 16.5%。
• 我們貸款組合預測淨現金流減少 169.5 百萬美元，或減少 1.5%，較 2024 年的減少幅度為小。
• 本公司於 2025 年回購約 1,514,000 股，總計 725.4 百萬美元，相當於年初發行在外股數的 12.6%。
•新加入5,752家經銷商，至2025年時共有15,745家活躍經銷商，為我們歷年來在財曆年中活躍經銷商數量最高。
•230.8 百萬美元用於經銷商保留金及加速支付經銷商保留金給經銷商。
•74.2 百萬美元與先前披露法律事項相關的或有損失。
•2025 年 12 月 31 日為止，本公司擁有 1.7 十億美元不受限制的現金及現金等價物，以及未使用的可用循環信用線。
•12 個工作場所獎項，包括在 Great Place to Work® 排名 #34，以及《財富》雜誌的 100 家最佳工作公司® 名單，以及在 2025 年美國最佳工作場所 USA 名單中，1,000-2,499 名員工公司規模排名 #2。
2024 年度截至 12 月 31 日，合併淨收入為 247.9 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後 19.88 美元，與 2023 年同期的 286.1 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後 21.99 美元相比。合併淨收入減少主要是由於利息費用及信貸損失準備金增加，部分抵銷了融資費用增加的影響。我們 2024 年度截至 12 月 31 日的結果包括：
•貸款組合的平均餘額為 7.5 十億美元，較 2023 年成長 13.6%。

headings: 產業、營運及總體經濟風險
本公司無法準確預測及估算未來收款金額與時間，可能對營運結果產生重大不利影響。
由於傳統融資來源與非傳統貸款機構的競爭，本公司可能無法成功競爭。
依賴第三方管理本公司附加產品業務，可能對本公司營運與財務結果產生不利影響。
本公司依賴高階管理階層，若失去任何一位高階管理人員或無法聘請更多團隊成員，可能對本公司獲利能力產生不利影響。
本公司聲譽為業務重要資產，而本公司業務可能受市場對本公司看法的影響。
傳染性疾病爆發或其他公共衛生緊急事件，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性及營運結果產生重大且不利的影響。
經紀商集中於數個州，可能對本公司產生不利影響。
對我們委外業務功能的依賴可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們聘僱及留住外籍工程人員的能力可能會受到移民限制的影響。
由於目前的經濟情況，我們可能無法執行我們的業務策略。
政府或市場對氣候變遷及相關環境議題的回應，可能會對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
資金與流動性風險
我們可能無法持續取得或更新資金來源，並獲得維持及擴張業務所需的資金。
我們債務的條款會限制我們如何進行業務活動。
違反我們的定期資產支持證券融資或倉儲設施條款，可能會對我們的營運產生重大不利影響。
本公司重大債務可能對營運造成負面影響，使本公司無法履行債務義務，並對財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司可能無法產生足夠現金流量以償還現有債務並支應營運資金，並可能被迫採取其他行動以履行債務義務。
利率波動可能對本公司借款成本、獲利能力及流動性產生不利影響。
本公司信用評級降低可能提高本公司從資本市場籌資的成本，並限制本公司對資本市場的存取，進而對流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司可能產生 substantially more 債務及其他負債。這可能會進一步加劇現有債務水準所伴隨的風險。
科技與網路安全風險
本公司對科技的依賴可能對營運產生重大不利影響。
本公司使用電子契約可能影響本公司對消費者貸款的所有權或質權的確立能力。
未能妥善保護我們的專有商業資訊或 confidential consumer 及 team member 個人資訊，可能使我們面臨責任，降低我們的獲利能力，並損害我們的聲譽。
人工智慧的開發與應用帶來風險與挑戰，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
法律與法規風險
我們偶爾參與的訴訟可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生不利影響。
稅法的變更及不確定所得稅事項的解決，可能對我們的營運成果及營運現金流產生重大不利影響。
我們所受或可能受的法規，可能對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 本公司所取得的消費貸款多數係針對信用紀錄不良或信用紀錄有限之個人。針對這些個人所發放之消費貸款，通常具有較高之違約風險、違約風險及收回風險，以及較高之損失率，與針對信用紀錄較佳之消費者所發放之貸款相比。由於本公司大部分之營業收入及營運現金流係來自這些消費貸款，因此本公司準確預測消費貸款表現之能力對本公司之業務及財務結果至關重要。於取得時，本公司預測消費貸款之未來預期現金流。根據這些預測，包括預估車輛被收回並出售時之整批車輛價格，本公司會向相關經銷商支付預付或一次性買斷金額，以達到最大化經濟利潤，為非GAAP財務指標。本公司持續預測每筆消費貸款於取得後之預期回收率。這些預測亦為本公司會計處理認列融資費用收入及決定信用損失撥備之關鍵假設。請參閱本表10-K第7項「關鍵會計估計－融資費用收入及信用損失撥備」節，此節已於本文件中引用。任何單筆消費貸款之實際現金流常與取得時預估之現金流不同。無法保證本公司之預測將準確，或消費貸款表現將如預期。在經濟條件變動之期間，準確預測消費貸款表現更具挑戰性。若本公司整體預測不準確，本公司之財務狀況、流動性及營運結果可能受到重大不利影響。

不具資格取得傳統汽車貸款之消費者之汽車融資市場規模龐大且競爭激烈。此市場由多種公司服務，包括「買這裡、付這裡」經銷商。此市場目前亦由銀行、汽車製造商之附屬融資機構、信用合作社及公私營獨立融資公司服務。許多這些公司規模較大且擁有較多財務資源，而本公司所能取得之財務資源較少，且許多公司與汽車經銷商有長期合作關係。汽車融資提供者傳統上以所收取之利率、所接受之信用品質、所提供的貸款條款之靈活性及對經銷商與消費者之服務品質來競爭。本公司可能無法在汽車融資市場中成功競爭，或因此市場競爭激烈，本公司之營運結果、現金流及財務狀況可能因應競爭壓力調整業務而受到重大不利影響。提高貸款之預付比率會降低本公司預期在貸款上所賺取之資本回報率。此外，若本公司無法維持並擴大與經銷商之關係，則可能無法接受預期之貸款數量及條款。
不利之經濟條件、汽車或融資產業、或非優質消費者市場之變化，可能對本公司之財務狀況、流動性及營運結果造成不利影響，影響本公司所依賴之關鍵供應商提供服務之能力，以及本公司未來進行融資交易之能力。

本公司受制於一般經濟條件，而此等條件為本公司所無法控制。在經濟減速或衰退期間，本公司之消費貸款之違約、違約、收回及損失可能增加，而消費貸款之提前償還，歷來在消費者信貸較少可得之期間較低，可能下降。此等期間通常亦伴隨消費者對汽車之需求減少及汽車之價值下降，此會削弱擔保品之覆蓋程度並增加在違約時之損失金額。在經濟衰退期間，使用汽車之庫存量大幅增加，亦可能壓低收回之汽車之銷售價格或延遲這些銷售之時機。此外，通貨膨脹、汽油價格上漲、學生貸款償還之延後或恢復、對氣候相關計畫及規範之關注增加、股市價值下跌、不穩定之房地產價值、調整利率房貸轉為較高利率、失業率上升、消費者信貸之普遍可得性、關稅或其它影響消費者信心或可支配所得之因素，可能增加損失頻率並降低消費者對汽車之需求，同時削弱汽車之擔保價值。對美國進口課徵關稅或增加關稅，可能導致美國之二手車價格上漲，導致經銷商減少發放消費貸款，並導致本公司取得之消費貸款減少。由於本公司之業務聚焦於無法取得傳統汽車貸款之消費者，因此本公司之消費貸款之實際違約率、違約率、收回率及損失率可能高於一般汽車融資產業所經驗之情形，且可能因一般經濟衰退而更顯著地受到影響。

本公司依賴經銷商為本公司之計畫發放消費貸款。因一般經濟衰退或其他原因導致經銷商流失率高，可能對本公司之營運造成重大不利影響。此外，本公司依賴供應商提供本公司營運所需之服務。若因這些服務之供應延遲或中斷而影響本公司營運，可能對本公司營運造成重大不利影響。最後，在經濟減速或衰退期間，本公司之服務成本可能增加，而融資費用收入未相應增加。任何持續之增加違約、違約、收回或損失，或服務成本增加，亦可能對本公司之財務狀況、流動性及營運結果造成重大不利影響，並影響本公司未來進行融資交易之能力。
科技進步或汽車產業趨勢之變動，例如新自動駕駛技術或汽車及計程車共享計畫，可能降低消費者對汽車之需求。消費者對汽車之需求減少，可能對本公司之融資計畫之需求造成負面影響，同時削弱汽車之擔保價值，可能對本公司之財務狀況、流動性及營運結果造成重大不利影響。
